History of Present Illness:
46-year-old man. Thirty hours of increasing right lower abdominal pain and anorexia. He reports no prior abdominal operations.

Physical Examination:
Right lower-quadrant guarding and pain with movement; no distension. Temperature 37.4 C; heart rate 106/min; BP 116/78 mmHg; respiratory rate 22/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 15.1 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.9 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 276 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 138 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 4.1 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 117 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 40 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 30 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 25 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 101 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
CT abdomen/pelvis: 13 mm appendix containing an appendicolith, with wall enhancement and surrounding inflammation. No abscess or free air.
